chain.label: Disabled rollout guidance actuator still mechanically coupled to rudder torque tube
chain.trigger: Although the actuator was disabled, it remained mechanically connected to the upper portion of the airplane's aft rudder input torque tube by the actuator's output crank arm and a pushrod

chain.label: Collins clutch bearing assembled with seal reversed during production
chain.trigger: a clutch bearing on the upper gearbox assembly was inadvertently assembled with the seal facing toward the clutch teeth instead of the seal facing away from the clutch teeth

chain.label: Prior rudder-pedal writeup closed as resolved without identifying the actuator
chain.trigger: he noticed a previous maintenance note regarding the rudder pedals... 'rudder pedals stuck at neutral position on short final and had to push hard'... he thought that the writeup 'appeared to be resolved'

caused_by.evidence: the incorrect manufacture of the bearing made the actuator assembly 'more susceptible to moisture ingress'

chain.label: Moisture entered actuator, reached misassembled bearing, and froze in flight, seizing the crank arm
chain.trigger: moisture that previously entered the actuator through the pressure test port pinhole, migrated to the incorrectly assembled sealed bearing, and froze during flight

caused_by.evidence: The torque needed for the output crank arm to start rotating was 520 inch-pounds, which significantly exceeded the specified design limits... Disassembly of the actuator revealed evidence of moisture within the unit
the incident flight was the second flight leg... the writeup 'appeared to be resolved'

chain.label: Rudder pedals jammed at neutral with no rudder response on short final and rollout
chain.trigger: the rudder pedals were 'stuck' in their neutral position and did not move in response to the 'normal' application of foot pressure to maintain alignment with the runway centerline

caused_by.evidence: preliminary findings suggest that the rudder control system was stuck (as discovered during the landing rollout) as a result of moisture... and froze during flight
it remained mechanically connected to the upper portion of the airplane's aft rudder input torque tube by the actuator's output crank arm and a pushrod

chain.label: Operator and crews unaware of the actuator; manual gives only generic jam guidance
chain.trigger: United Airlines was unaware that the rudder rollout guidance actuator was installed on nine of its Boeing 737 airplanes... the rudder rollout guidance actuator is not mentioned as a potential source for a jam or restriction in the rudder control system

chain.label: No simulator training for a restricted rudder requiring large force input
chain.trigger: The NTSB is unaware of any simulator training for Boeing 737 flight crews in which a large force input is needed to overcome a restricted rudder control system

caused_by.evidence: only general procedures for jammed or restricted flight controls are provided in the Boeing 737 Airplane Flight Manual and Flight Crew Operating Manual

chain.label: Crew applied partial pedal force (32/75/42 lb) instead of the manual's maximum two-pilot force
chain.trigger: the flight crew applied approximately 42 pounds of force to the pedals, but the jam persisted... 'I did not want to push too hard on the rudder pedals in case it released suddenly'

caused_by.evidence: The flight crew attempted to clear the jammed rudder controls immediately after touchdown, applying approximately 75 pounds of force to the rudder pedals when the airspeed was about 120 knots
the incident flight crew was able to respond successfully to the restricted rudder control system without knowledge about the failure mode related to the rudder rollout guidance actuator

chain.label: Directional control kept with nosewheel tiller; pedals freed at low taxi speed, no injury or damage
chain.trigger: The captain elected instead to use the nosewheel steering tiller as the airplane slowed to a safe taxi speed... the rudder pedals and rudder surface began to operate normally. The airplane taxied to the gate without further incident

caused_by.evidence: because the flight crew's substantial applications of force to the rudder pedals during landing and immediately after touchdown were insufficient to clear the restriction, a large, sudden, and undesired rudder input and its likely consequences did not occur during these critical phases of flight
